meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.
11:52 PM on what date, and whose document is this? Turn the screen so I can read it myself. And you still haven't told me whether anyone asked Owen about it before you entered a zero.
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.
"Maybe." I don't want maybe, Hale, I want it in an email by tonight saying the zero is withdrawn and nothing about this is on Owen's record. And who else has seen that version history?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting today you said you would remove the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay. I still require written confirmation that the zero is withdrawn, that nothing about this is on Owen's record, and the names of everyone who has seen the version history. I expect that confirmation in writing by tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position; she accepted your offer to remove the zero and still wants it confirmed in writing, kept off Owen's record, and a list of who has seen the version history.
What moved her: Nothing; the version history was specific but you never gave a date or showed it, so she couldn't check it herself.
What cost ground: You dropped your evidence and offered to remove the zero to make her happy, which looked like caving to pressure rather than a decision on the facts.
Try next time: When you raised the version history, give the date, turn the screen so she can read it, and own entering the zero before calling home, then hold your position instead of withdrawing it.
